Security Design: Waypoint Access Control

Two actors reach Waypoint's job data: the Field Technician Actor, the crew member in the field, and the Dispatcher Actor at the desk. The Field Technician Actor is assigned to the Technician Role and accesses the Job Record, the secure resource that holds a customer's address and payment history. Before any of that, the Field Technician Actor requires the Technician Auth Config, the authentication config that establishes who they are.

Roles carry the privileges. The Technician Role aggregates the Job View Permission and authorizes that same Job View Permission for read-only work. The Job View Permission authorizes the Read Job Operation, the resource operation a technician may perform, and that operation accesses the Job Record while being constrained by the Job Access Condition. The Job Access Condition, an access condition, constrains the Job View Permission and references the Job Record it applies to.

All of this is anchored by policy. The Least Privilege Policy Rule authorizes the Job View Permission, protects the Job Record, uses the Job Access Condition, and composes the Waypoint Access Policy. That Waypoint Access Policy, a security policy, aggregates the Least Privilege Policy Rule, governs the Job Record, and constrains the Job View Permission so no role can quietly widen its own reach. The Technician Auth Config authenticates the Field Technician Actor, protects the Job Record, and is constrained by the Waypoint Access Policy.
